results.corrected_extracted: Examinations were done by experienced sonographers who were not told the person's identity; images were stored, randomized and read blind by one sonographer and one independent observer, whose agreement on the FDA criteria was excellent (kappa above 0.9); the independent observer's data were used. Valve disease was defined by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) criteria for appetite-suppressant-induced valve disease: mitral regurgitation of moderate or greater severity (2/4 or more) or aortic regurgitation of mild or greater severity (1/4 or more); Fisher's exact test was used for the FDA score. Results: 33 people who took MDMA and 29 controls were selected, none with a history of cardiac disease; 4 people in the MDMA group were excluded after scanning (3 for inadequate image quality, 1 for mitral and tricuspid prolapse), leaving 29; all had used MDMA for at least 6 months. 8 people (28%) who took MDMA met the FDA criteria and none of the controls (p = 0.0045); mitral, aortic and tricuspid regurgitation and shape abnormalities were more often seen in the MDMA group (Table 1).

results.corrected_extracted: As summarized by the review: in 8 volunteers given 1.0 and 1.6 mg/kg (Kolbrich and colleagues) the ear-temperature rise after MDMA (+0.3 and +0.4 degrees Celsius; temperature also rose under placebo) was not significantly different from placebo, but the link between blood MDMA and temperature rise was (p < 0.0001). At a dance party, 27 people (Irvine and colleagues) were measured the evening before, at 4 am and at 10 am: the rise was about +0.2 and not significant, there was no control night so the fall of body temperature during the night was not accounted for, 5 people had particularly high blood MDMA, and the two people with the highest levels (0.77 and 0.84 mg/l) had the largest individual rises (+1.0 and +1.6 degrees); across the group the link between blood level and rise was borderline (r = +0.38, p = 0.058). Methamphetamine and cannabis were present in 41% and 33% of the group.
